Epoch AI LLM inference prices have fallen rapidly
AI Index 2024 training costs GPT-4 78 million Gemini Ultra 191 million

sources_considered.why: Primary OpenAI announcement of GPT-4o pricing, May 2024.
Independent analysis of price trends at fixed capability; context on whether cuts reflect margins.
Reports AI Index estimates of rising training costs; context for the total-cost reading.
read_page did not return the figures.

receipt.public_excerpt: GPT‑4 Turbo input tokens are 3x cheaper than GPT‑4 at $0.01 and output tokens are 2x cheaper at $0.03.

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI cut the price of its GPT-4-class model 2-3x per token in November 2023, which OpenAI described as more capable. That is a material fall in the unit cost of use within the period.

metric_scope.metric: API price per token for comparable-capability models

receipt.public_excerpt: It matches GPT‑4 Turbo performance on text in English and code, with significant improvement on text in non-English languages, while also being much faster and 50% cheaper in the API.

evidence_items.explanation: Eight weeks before the post, OpenAI halved the API price again for a model it says matches GPT-4 Turbo. Together with e1, comparable output got several times cheaper within the period.

metric_scope.metric: API price per token for comparable-capability models

evidence_items.locator: section Learn more about this graph, paragraph 2

receipt.public_excerpt: Reduced profit margins may explain some of the drops in price, but we didn’t find clear evidence for this.

evidence_items.explanation: An independent analysis found falling prices at fixed capability. It found no clear evidence that the falls were just thinner margins, which eases the worry that price is a poor proxy for cost.

receipt.public_excerpt: The report estimated that OpenAI’s GPT-4 likely cost $78 million to train, while Google’s Gemini Ultra had an estimated price tag of upward of $191 million.

evidence_items.explanation: Training costs for frontier models were rising. Under a total-cost reading this fits his view, but it measures a different thing (training spend per model) than the unit cost of use.

metric_scope.metric: estimated compute cost to train a frontier model

unresolved_gaps: Providers' internal serving costs are not public; list prices are a proxy.
Under a total-spending reading (training and capex), costs rose, so the result depends on reading 'costs' as unit cost of use.
